step_by_step_reasoning: The New York Times architecture uses AWS Control Tower to manage multi-account environments. Developers push container images to Amazon ECR within developer accounts, which are then deployed to a centralized Amazon EKS cluster in a runtime account. For runtime data access, the EKS cluster routes traffic via AWS Transit Gateway back to backend services such as Amazon S3 and Amazon RDS hosted in the developer accounts.

graph.name: The New York Times Multi-Account Governance and Centralized Kubernetes Runtime Environment
graph.notes: Architecture showcases multi-account governance using Control Tower, container deployments from ECR to centralized EKS runtime, and cross-account service communication through Transit Gateway.

nodes.name: Transit Gateway

edges.notes: Developer pushes container images to ECR via CI/CD pipeline.
CI/CD deploys container image from ECR to EKS runtime cluster.
EKS workloads send outbound requests through Transit Gateway.
Transit Gateway routes traffic to S3 and other services inside individual developer accounts.
Control Tower vends developer accounts and applies security policies across resources.
